title: DOJ Criminal Investigation of Fed Chair Powell Sparks Bipartisan Backlash
subtitle: The Justice Department served Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell with grand jury subpoenas threatening criminal indictment over his congressional testimony about building renovations. Powell called it a 'pretext' to pressure the Fed on interest rates. Several Republican senators vowed to block Trump's Fed nominees, while Democrats accused Trump of acting like a 'wannabe dictator.'

conservative.headline: Holding the Fed Accountable: DOJ Investigates Powell's Testimony on $2.5 Billion Building Boondoggle
conservative.byline: As seen on Fox News, Washington Examiner, and The Hill
paragraphs: The Department of Justice has opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over his June 2025 testimony to the Senate Banking Committee regarding the central bank's controversial $2.5 billion headquarters renovation — a project that has ballooned hundreds of millions over budget.

Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-FL), who first referred Powell to the DOJ in July 2025, said in a statement: "These are not minor misstatements. Chairman Powell knowingly misled both Congress and executive branch officials about the true nature of a taxpayer-funded project. Lying under oath is a serious offense — especially from someone tasked with overseeing our monetary system and public trust."

Luna's referral cited Powell's sworn testimony in which he denied the inclusion of luxury features — such as a VIP dining room, premium marble, water features, and a rooftop terrace garden — in the renovation. According to Luna, official project documents submitted to the National Capital Planning Commission directly contradicted his statements.

President Trump told NBC News on Sunday that he had no knowledge of the subpoenas but added: "He's certainly not very good at the Fed, and he's not very good at building buildings." When asked if the investigation was related to interest rates, Trump said: "No. I wouldn't even think of doing it that way. What should pressure him is the fact that rates are far too high. That's the only pressure he's got."

U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia Jeanine Pirro defended the investigation on X, writing: "The United States Attorney's Office contacted the Federal Reserve on multiple occasions to discuss cost overruns and the chairman's congressional testimony, but were ignored, necessitating the use of legal process — which is not a threat. The word 'indictment' has come out of Mr. Powell's mouth, no one else's."

Rep. Nick LaLota (R-NY) told The Hill: "It's just an investigation, at this point. It's not an indictment. And Jerome Powell…is advocating for $2.5 billion of costs. That's more than a Yankee Stadium, for a federal office building. I think that's worthy of investigation. Certainly, if he lied to Congress, that's worthy of an investigation."

White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said the president "has every right to criticize the Fed chair. He has a First Amendment right, just like all of you do. And one thing's for sure the president's made it quite clear, is Jerome Powell is bad at his job. As for whether or not Jerome Powell is a criminal, that's an answer the Department of Justice is going to have to find out."
National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett told reporters: "I would expect that the markets would be happy to see that there's more transparency at the Fed."

On the far right, Rep. Eric Burlison (R-MO), a member of the House Freedom Caucus, told The Hill: "I have long said the Fed needs to be audited, and I would even support ending it. I'm not a fan of the Federal Reserve. We've turned over a large part of our economy and a lot of major decisions over to this entity that is not accountable to the taxpayers whatsoever."

However, not all Republicans backed the investigation. Sen. Thom Tillis (R-NC) issued a statement saying: "If there were any remaining doubt whether advisers within the Trump Administration are actively pushing to end the independence of the Federal Reserve, there should now be none. It is now the independence and credibility of the Department of Justice that are in question." Tillis vowed to "oppose the confirmation of any nominee for the Fed — including the upcoming Fed Chair vacancy — until this legal matter is fully resolved."

liberal.headline: Trump Weaponizes DOJ Against Fed Chair in 'Unprecedented' Attack on Central Bank Independence
liberal.byline: As seen on CNN, MSNBC, and PBS NewsHour
paragraphs: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell revealed Sunday that the Justice Department served the central bank with grand jury subpoenas threatening criminal indictment — an action he called a politically motivated attack on the Fed's independence from the White House.

In an extraordinary video statement, Powell said: "No one — certainly not the chair of the Federal Reserve — is above the law. But this unprecedented action should be seen in the broader context of the administration's threats and ongoing pressure." He added: "The threat of criminal charges is a consequence of the Federal Reserve setting interest rates based on our best assessment of what will serve the public, rather than following the preferences of the President."

Powell explicitly rejected the stated rationale for the investigation, saying: "This new threat is not about my testimony last June or about the renovation of the Federal Reserve buildings. This is about whether the Fed will be able to continue to set interest rates based on evidence and economic conditions — or whether instead monetary policy will be directed by political pressure or intimidation." He concluded: "Public service sometimes requires standing firm in the face of threats."

Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) said Trump's "assault on the Fed's independence continues," adding: "This is the kind of bullying that we've all come to expect from Donald Trump and his cronies. Anyone who is independent and doesn't just fall in line behind Trump gets investigated. Jay Powell and the Fed aren't the reason Trump's economy and his poll numbers are in the toilet. If he's looking for the person who caused that he should look in the mirror."

Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), ranking member of the Senate Banking Committee, said in a speech at the National Press Club: "Acting like the wannabe dictator he is, Trump is trying to push out the chairman of the Federal Reserve Board and complete his corrupt takeover of America's central bank so that it serves his interests, along with his billionaire friends." Warren said the Senate should not "move forward with any Trump nominee for the Fed, including Fed Chair."

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD), top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, wrote to Chairman Jim Jordan requesting a congressional inquiry, calling it "a sham criminal investigation" and "a flagrant attempt by the President to bully and intimidate the Board into setting interest rates not based on evidence, economic conditions, or the mandate given to the Board by Congress, but rather to please the president."

A bipartisan group of 13 former Fed chairs and top economists — including Ben Bernanke, Janet Yellen, and Alan Greenspan — issued a joint statement calling the probe "an unprecedented attempt to use prosecutorial attacks to undermine" Fed independence. The statement warned: "This is how monetary policy is made in emerging markets with weak institutions, with highly negative consequences for inflation and the functioning of their economies more broadly. It has no place in the United States whose greatest strength is the rule of law, which is at the foundation of our economic success."

Fed Governor Michael Barr called the investigation "an assault on the independence of the Fed," while Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee described Powell as a "first-ballot hall of fame Fed chair."
Jason Furman, Harvard economist and former Obama economic advisor, told reporters: "I think this is ham-handed, counter-productive, and going to set back the president's cause."

Notably, Republican Senators Thom Tillis (NC) and Lisa Murkowski (AK) broke with Trump to defend Powell. Murkowski said: "After speaking with Chair Powell this morning, it's clear the administration's investigation is nothing more than an attempt at coercion."

House Financial Services Committee Chair French Hill (R-AR) also criticized the investigation: "I know Mr. Powell to be a man of integrity with a strong commitment to public service. While over the years we have had our policy disagreements, I found him to be forthright, candid, and a person of the highest integrity. Pursuing criminal charges relating to his testimony on building renovations at a time when the nation's economy requires focus creates an unnecessary distraction."

paragraphs: WHAT'S ACTUALLY HAPPENING:

✓ The DOJ investigation is real and stems from Rep. Anna Paulina Luna's July 2025 criminal referral to Attorney General Pam Bondi alleging Powell committed perjury during his June 2025 Senate testimony about the Fed's headquarters renovation. The probe is being led by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro. Powell confirmed receiving grand jury subpoenas on January 10, 2026. Source: NBC News

✓ Both sides acknowledge the Fed's renovation costs have risen significantly — from an original estimate of $1.9 billion to approximately $2.5 billion. Powell has disputed some characterizations of the project's features in his congressional testimony and ordered an inspector general review. Source: CNBC

✓ Trump told NBC News he had no advance knowledge of the subpoenas. However, he had publicly previewed potential legal action on December 29, 2025, saying: "We're thinking about bringing a suit against Powell for incompetence." Source: CBS News
CONSERVATIVE SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Claim: Powell "knowingly misled" Congress. This remains unproven. Disputed testimony isn't automatically perjury — prosecutors must prove intentional falsehood, not mere error or difference of interpretation. Luna's referral cites contradictions but hasn't been tested in court.

✓ Fair point: The $2.5 billion renovation cost is substantial and questions about congressional testimony deserve scrutiny. The Fed, like any institution, should be accountable for public statements. Project costs did rise significantly from original estimates.
LIBERAL SPIN VS. REALITY:

⚠️ Calling Trump a "wannabe dictator" over this specific action is rhetorical escalation. However, concerns about Fed independence are legitimate — the timing after a year of Trump attacking Powell over rates raises real questions about motives.

✓ Fair point: Criminal prosecution of a Fed chair over building testimony is unprecedented. Bipartisan economic experts, including Republican-appointed former Fed chairs, have condemned the probe. Several Republican senators who typically support Trump called it "coercion." Source: PBS NewsHour
WHAT BOTH SIDES AREN'T TELLING YOU:

Powell explicitly framed the investigation as being about interest rate policy, not building costs. Trump has publicly demanded lower interest rates throughout his second term, calling Powell "too late" and a "political hack." The Fed cut rates three times in late 2025 but has signaled a pause. Whether the investigation is genuinely about testimony accuracy or pressure on monetary policy remains a matter of interpretation. Source: Federal Reserve
BOTTOM LINE:

The investigation is real, the renovation cost disputes are legitimate, but the unprecedented nature of criminally investigating a Fed chair over building testimony — combined with Trump's year-long public pressure campaign on rates — gives credence to Powell's claim that this is about more than construction costs. The bipartisan backlash from economists and even some Republican senators suggests this may backfire politically.
